note: The RPC surface set the Potpie daemon serves at POST /rpc and POST /attr.
This file is the pinned copy: tests/unit/test_rpc_surface_manifest.py asserts
potpie.daemon.surfaces.RPC_SURFACES equals it, so widening or narrowing the
allowlist cannot happen without a deliberate edit here — and a reviewer sees
the served API change as a change to a contract file rather than as one word
The set is maintained twice. The managed service (github.com/potpie-ai/pie)
runs its own build of this daemon with its own copy, they drifted once, and
the drift was invisible until 'potpie doctor' turned out to be dead against
managed because 'resources' was missing there. That repo does not import this
one (it depends on potpie-context-engine, not on the potpie product package),
so the copies are compared by reading its source: the same test parses
managed_copy.symbol out of managed_copy.path when a checkout is reachable, and
skips with a reason when it is not.
At runtime the daemon publishes this same set at GET /surfaces, and the CLI
reads it once per connection (potpie/daemon/negotiation.py) so a refusal is
classified against what a host says it serves rather than against the wording
of its error. The managed service has no such route yet — until it does, a
surface it omits is still recognised only by its sentence.
